pf2e-customizations.lockPicking.instruct: Drag each pin to rotate it. It'll resist and shudder as you push it without finding the notch; ease off before it fights back too long and it'll hold its ground safely. Find the spot where it turns freely, then click Set Pin. Pushing too hard for too long snaps it back to start and costs you a mistake — too many mistakes and the pick breaks. Give Up at any time to walk away with a safe failure instead of risking that.

pf2e-customizations.timelinePuzzle.instr: Once you start, you'll see clues about the true order of a set of events. Drag the event blocks (or use the arrow buttons) to put them in chronological order, using the clues as your guide. Click Check Order any time to test your current arrangement — a wrong guess costs nothing, so try freely. The clock starts the moment you click Begin, so make sure you're ready first; the faster you solve it, the better the outcome.

pf2e-customizations.alibiMatrix.instruct: Once you start, you'll see a set of clues about who was where (and why). Click a grid cell to cycle it through blank, ✗ (impossible), and ✓ (true) — use the clues to cross out impossible pairings and confirm the real ones. Click Check Matrix any time to test your current grid — a wrong guess costs nothing, so try freely. The clock starts the moment you click Begin, so make sure you're ready first; the faster you solve it, the better the outcome.

pf2e-customizations.factSifter.instructi: Once you start, you'll see a shuffled list of fragments — some form a connected chain of genuine, mutually-supporting facts; the rest are deceptive noise, either directly contradicting one specific detail in a true fact (a different color, number, or name for the same thing) or simply irrelevant. The exact number of true fragments you need to find is shown above the list, along with a live counter as you select. Look for a specific, repeated detail that shows up in more than one fragment — if it's echoed by another fragment, it's likely part of the true thread; if a fragment stands alone with no matching detail anywhere else, it's likely a decoy. Sometimes a Lead is shown above the fragments — that's a fact the investigation has already confirmed, not something to sift; use its detail the same way you'd use one found by matching two fragments to each other. Click a fragment to highlight it as one you believe is true; click again to un-highlight it. Click Confirm Findings any time to test your current selection — a wrong guess costs nothing, so try freely. The clock starts the moment you click Begin, so make sure you're ready first; the faster you solve it, the better the outcome.
